description:
Redwood Inference will stand up a reliable, repeatable sales demo environment (“demo tenant”) containing a small set of known-good scenarios that showcase the platform’s differentiators (latency/cost controls, reliability/fallback, deployment flexibility, and observability) and pair it with a scripted talk track and a standard demo deck.

Goals:
- Create a demo tenant that is stable, fast to reset, and safe to use live with prospects (no surprises, no sensitive data).
- Provide 4–6 “known-good” demo scenarios with canned inputs, expected outputs, and failure-mode fallbacks.
- Produce a repeatable talk track (speaker notes + objection handling) aligned to personas (ML/platform eng, security, procurement).
- Provide a single source of truth for demo setup, runbook, and ownership; reduce reliance on ad-hoc SE heroics.

Scope (in):
- Demo tenant configuration (models, routing/fallback rules, quotas/rate limits, dashboards).
- Seed data + scenario scripts (prompt sets, example requests, expected outputs).
- A standard deck + talk track + “choose-your-own-adventure” branches.
- Enablement materials: checklist, FAQ, and troubleshooting/runbook.

Scope (out):
- Building a full customer POC framework or bespoke industry demos for every vertical.
- Major product feature work beyond light demo-oriented fixes and documentation/examples.

Primary stakeholders:
- Exec sponsor: Jordan Blake (CRO)
- Sales leadership: Stephanie Nguyen (VP Sales, NA), Lukas Meyer (VP Sales, EMEA)
- Solutions Engineering: Markus Klein (Dir. Solutions Engineering)
- Product Marketing: Soojin Lee (Dir. Product Marketing)
- Marketing: Camila Reyes (VP Marketing)
- Cross-functional support: DevEx/Platform/SRE (consulted for reliability, tenant automation, dashboards)

Phases & timeline (typical 6–8 weeks):
1) Requirements & scenario selection (week 1): define personas, “must-show” differentiators, and success criteria.
2) Demo tenant buildout (weeks 2–4): tenant config, seed data, scripted API calls, dashboards, reset automation, and guardrails.
3) Deck + talk track (weeks 3–6): iterative drafts, internal dry runs, objection handling, security slides.
4) Enablement & rollout (weeks 6–8): train AEs/SEs, publish runbook/FAQ, bake into sales process; measure demo-to-eval conversion and demo reliability.

Key deliverables:
- Demo tenant runbook + reset checklist + ownership/on-call rotation for demo incidents.
- Scripted scenarios (CLI or notebook + “expected outputs”) and “plan B” for live failures.
- Final deck and talk track, with variants for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- CRM workflow guidance: when to use demo tenant vs spinning up a prospect-specific trial.

Constraints/risks:
- Reliability: live demos must avoid flaky model availability, quota surprises, and dashboard lag.
- Security: tenant must be sanitized and access-controlled; no customer data; safe logging.
- Consistency: ensure scripts stay in sync with product changes (release notes + regression checks).

files.description: Canonical internal Confluence page describing the “Standard Demo Deck v1”: slide-by-slide intent, required screenshots, and which personas each section targets.
Master talk track script with timing, transitions, persona branches (platform eng vs ML eng vs security), and guidance on when to pivot from Hosted to Dedicated/Private.
FAQ for common security questions during demos: data retention, logging, encryption, SSO/SAML/RBAC posture, and how the demo tenant is isolated/sanitized.
Objection handling notes with competitive framing (latency/cost/reliability, deployment modes), including “what we show live” vs “what we claim” guidance.
Runbook for creating/updating the demo tenant: required configs, model/version pinning, routing/fallback rules, dashboards to verify, and rollback steps.
Operational doc for demo tenant monitoring: key dashboards, alert thresholds (latency/5xx/throttles), and who gets paged in business hours.
Lightweight PRD for the demo environment: success metrics (demo reliability rate, setup time), scenario requirements, and dependencies on engineering teams.
ADR documenting how demo scenarios pin model versions/quantization profiles, and the policy for updating them without breaking the talk track.
Working slide deck draft (slides) with iterative edits, placeholders for screenshots, and internal reviewer comments across Sales, SE, and PMM.
Collaborative doc with the live-demo narration, including exact phrases, click-path instructions in Console, and “if asked…” sidebars.
Sheet listing scenarios (e.g., streaming chat, tool calling, fallback routing, cost controls), required setup, expected outputs, and regression status.
One-page checklist for pre-demo and post-demo steps: quotas, seed data reset, dashboard sanity checks, and backup plan actions.
Doc collecting screenshot stubs/links and annotations for the deck (routes, rollouts, cost dashboard, error analysis) with version tracking.
Brainstorm notes from Sales/SE on objections and best responses; includes fragments and links to competitive intel.
